title: The First Great Civilisations
summary: How life along great rivers led to cities, writing and laws in Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Indus Valley and China.

steps.title: Why rivers?
sentences: Long ago people moved from hunting and gathering to farming.
Rivers gave water, rich soil and an easy way to travel.
So the first big cities grew beside rivers.

steps.title: Four river valleys
sentences: Mesopotamia grew between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, in what is now Iraq.
Egypt grew along the Nile, the Indus Valley civilisation along the Indus and nearby rivers, and ancient China along the Yellow River.
These all began roughly between five thousand and four thousand years ago.

steps.title: What they invented
sentences: Mesopotamians made one of the first writing systems, called cuneiform, pressed into clay.
Egyptians built pyramids and used a calendar based on the Nile's floods.
The Indus cities such as Mohenjo-daro and Harappa had straight streets, brick houses and drains.

steps.title: Still to learn
sentences: We can read Egyptian and Mesopotamian writing, but nobody has fully read the Indus script yet.
So much about how the Indus people lived is learned from objects they left behind.
Historians and archaeologists keep finding new clues.
points: Indus script is not yet read

facts: Harappan cities used standard-sized bricks and had covered drains over four thousand years ago.
The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest human-made structure in the world for about 3,800 years.
The Indus Valley people used carefully made weights for trade.

quiz.q: Why did early cities grow beside rivers?
options: Water, rich soil and easy travel
quiz.why: Farming needs water and soil, and rivers helped travel and trade.

quiz.q: Which river is linked to ancient Egypt?
quiz.why: Ancient Egypt grew along the Nile.

quiz.q: What is true about the Indus script?
options: It has not been fully read yet
quiz.why: Scholars are still trying to understand the Indus script.

notes: Dates are approximate and given as round numbers.
